title: Acme Health priv-deploy timeout breadcrumbs
content:
Scratchpad - Acme Health private deployment timeout / request failures (notes + draft comms)

Summary:
- Customer: Acme Health (private deployment in us-east-1 VPC)
- Symptom: intermittent 504 / inference timeouts for chat completions starting ~2026-02-27 22:10 UTC. Spike in tail latency and some requests failing to complete.
- Impact: ~3% of requests returning 504s during peak window; customer reports user-facing errors in production.
- Current status: mitigation in progress, still seeing occasional timeouts. This doc is my running notes for triage and a rough draft for internal + customer comms.

Top-level hypothesis (working):
1) Networking egress/connection teardown between inference runtime (nginx front) and model worker (grpc local) causing long waits then 504s.
2) Redis prefix cache experiencing transient connection hits -> blocking request path (we use Redis for prefix cache in this deploy).
3) Autoscale jitter: workers being cycled during peak due to node pressure, causing cold-cache and KV misses -> long model compile times.

Quick timeline with fingerprints (UTC):
- 2026-02-27 21:58: customer first slack pinged: "saw errors around 21:50"
- 2026-02-27 22:10: monitoring alert: route /v1/chat/complete p95 latency > 8s, error rate 2.8%
- 2026-02-27 22:12: oncall @jenna started live-debugging; reproduced 504 via curl to gateway (see commands)
- 2026-02-27 22:18: scaled inference workers + pinned model variant to smaller sequence length (quick fallback)
- 2026-02-27 22:35: partial improvement, error rate down to 0.9% but tail still elevated
- 2026-02-28 03:00: another spike correlated with node OOM on node-17 (k8s evicted); restarted node, evicted pods replaced
- 2026-03-01 11:22: increased Redis connection error logs observed (see log snippets)
- 2026-03-04 ongoing: intermittent 504s continue at low volume; we have a reproducer and plan to run controlled load.

Commands tried (copied from shell history):
- curl reproducer (synthetic):
  curl -i -X POST https://acme-gw.example.com/v1/chat/complete -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"input":"hello"}' -m 15 -v
  -> observed: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
  -> curl exit code 28 after ~15s

- kubectl checks (from admin host):
  kubectl -n acme get pods -o wide | grep inference
  kubectl -n acme logs inference-worker-7f4b -c inference --since=10m | tail -n 200
  kubectl -n acme describe pod inference-worker-7f4b
  -> saw repeated: "grpc: the client connection is closing" and long GC pauses reported in JVM  (note: our worker is C++ but wrapper logs show GC-style pauses due to python shim)

- networking probes:
  curl -v --connect-timeout 3 http://10.42.5.72:8080/healthz
  -> returned 200 OK when checked, but at times the probe hung for ~10s
  traceroute -n 10.42.5.72
  -> no obvious routing loops inside VPC

- redis checks (from bastion):
  redis-cli -h redis.acme.internal PING
  -> PONG
  redis-cli -h redis.acme.internal --latency -c
  -> median ~1ms but occasional samples > 100ms during incident window
  grep -i \"connection refused\" /var/log/redis/redis-server.log | tail -n 50
  -> intermittent connections closed from ephemeral IPs (kube svc ips)

Key log snippets (sanitized):
- inference-worker stderr:
  [2026-02-27T22:11:05Z] WARN runtime/transport.go:204 upstream read error: read tcp 10.42.6.3:43210->10.42.5.72:8080: read: connection reset by peer
  [2026-02-27T22:12:09Z] ERROR router/handler.go:87 request 12345 took 12.7s to complete, exceeding SLO; fallback route triggered

- nginx gateway:
  10.42.1.11 - - [27/Feb/2026:22:11:04 +0000] "POST /v1/chat/complete HTTP/1.1" 504 173 "-" "curl/7.81.0"
  2026/02/27 22:11:04 [error] 3246#0: *832 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.42.1.11, server: _, request: "POST /v1/chat/complete HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.42.5.72:8080/", host: "acme-gw.example.com"

Observed patterns: 
- Most 504s occur during bursts of traffic or immediately after a pod restart.
- When Redis samples >50ms, the probability of a 504 increases in the next 30s.
- Node eviction (OOM) events preceded two of the major spikes.

Hypotheses detail:
- H1 (network teardown): kernel-level conntrack entries hitting table limits -> SYN/ESTABLISHED being dropped mid-flight. Evidence: intermittent socket reset messages and elevated conntrack stats on node-17 at 03:00. Need: /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count snapshots from node across time window.
- H2 (redis pressure causing sync wait): prefix cache misses + slow redis causing inference shim to wait on prefix fetch -> request blocking. Evidence: redis latency >100ms samples and correlation with spikes. Need: instrument redis client calls in worker to capture fetch durations.
- H3 (cold model / compile): model variant compile takes 6-10s after cold start; autoscaler may have removed warm workers. Evidence: model compile logs with timestamps aligning to errors. Need: confirm autoscaler activity logs.

Immediate mitigations applied so far:
- P1: pinned model variant to v1.2-smaller-seqlen for Acme (reduced compile time) — reduced p99 by ~1.2s
- P2: temporary increase in worker replica count during peak windows (manual scaling)
- P3: increased healthcheck frequency to detect slow pods earlier

What I still need to collect (action items):
- [ ] conntrack snapshots from node-17 for 2026-02-27 21:30 -> 2026-02-28 04:00 (ask infra: @Marcus to fetch via kexec/archives)
- [ ] worker-side Redis client latency traces (add brief hook to log fetch durations) - quick code change in repo infra/redis-metrics branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/782)
- [ ] autoscaler events for the namespace (kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp)
- [ ] reproduce with synthetic load that ramps to 120rps for 30s while forcing 10% simulated redis latency (use chaos-testing infra)

Notes-to-self about debugging steps to run next:
- instrument worker binary to log time spent on prefix cache fetch vs model forward. Add timing around redis GET calls and around model.load/compile steps. Build small image and deploy to a canary 1-pod subset.
- run tcpdump on node-17 during next reproducer to capture TCP resets (filter port 8080)
- verify kernel conntrack size: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and snapshot /proc/net/nf_conntrack

Draft internal comms (short) - to be refined before sending to CS/SEs:
Subject: Acme Health - ongoing intermittent 504s (priv deploy) - triage update
Hi CS/SE team,
Quick update: we're actively triaging intermittent 504s seen by Acme Health since 2026-02-27. Root cause not confirmed; current suspects are transient Redis latency impacting prefix cache and occasional node-level OOM/conntrack pressure leading to connection resets. We have applied temporary mitigations (pinned model variant, increased replica count) and error rate has decreased but not fully resolved.
Next steps: collect conntrack traces, add lightweight Redis latency logging in worker, and run controlled load with induced Redis latency to reproduce. Will follow with a more detailed timeline and ask for customer permission to run a short repro (5–10 minutes) during a maintenance window.
Thanks,
Jenna

Draft customer-facing message (very rough) - internal review required before sending:
Subject: Update: brief maintenance & troubleshooting for model latency
Hi [Customer contact],
We wanted to update you that our team has identified intermittent service timeouts impacting a small portion of inference requests in your private deployment. We have implemented short-term mitigations and are planning a brief, coordinated test (5–10 minutes) during a maintenance window to safely reproduce and fix the issue. This test will not change your data or models; it will only introduce controlled, low-volume traffic to help isolate the cause.
Would [Customer contact] be available for a 10-minute window tomorrow 14:00–14:30 UTC? Please let us know and we'll coordinate.

Questions / open items to raise to Eng/SRE forum:
- Can infra provide conntrack historical snapshots from node-17? (Marcus)
- Are we comfortable running a short chaos test that introduces 50–150ms latency to Redis in customer's VPC? Need CS approval and a runbook.
- Should we add a small fallback to serve last-known-good cache when Redis latency > 50ms to avoid blocking? Quick patch vs risk analysis.

Misc scratch lines (notes to self):
- remember to scrub keys/tokens before sharing logs
- check if Acme's KMS rotates keys nightly (could cause transient auth failures to redis?)
- add a quick Grafana panel for redis p50/p95 overlayed with 504 count for this deployment

-- end of scratchpad --

(If I don't get to this tomorrow: leave the reproducer running at 0.5rps to capture baseline, then ramp to 15rps during a quiet window and tcpdump on node-17)
